scenes.shots:
Scene title "Why can't a laptop run a 70B model?" fades in at 0.2s.
- 2.7s ("70 billion parameters"): the tall blue bar grows from the baseline (scaleY 0→1, transform-origin bottom, 1.6s power2.out); its "140 GB" label counts up 0→140 in sync (mono, tabular-nums) and "70B model · FP16" appears under it.
- 9.0s ("graphics card has 24"): the teal GPU outline box draws on (stroke-dashoffset) with "24 GB" counting up and "your GPU" under it.
- 10.5s: the red dashed line at the GPU top draws left→right and "won't fit" fades in; the blue bar gets a 2-frame red tint pulse (fill to #FC6255 at 25% blend then back) — subtle.
- 14.5s ("quantization"): "3.14159" types in digit by digit at right (blue mono).
- 18.6s ("Rounding."): the ↓ arrow draws, then the big yellow serif "3" pops (back.out) — this is the button of the scene.
Ambient: whole group drifts up 6px over the scene.

Scene title fades in at 0.2s.
- 4.2s ("$3.99"): "$3.99" (blue) fades up; at 5.8s the ↓ draws and "≈ $4" (yellow) pops.
- 8.0s ("52.7 kilometres"): the "52.7 km → ≈ 50 km" line types in (mono).
- 15.0s ("smooth colour gradient"): the smooth gradient bar wipes in left→right (clip-path inset or scaleX from left, 1.4s) with its label "millions of shades".
- 20.0s ("Squeeze it down to just 16"): the 16-band posterized bar wipes in left→right beneath it, band by band (stagger ≤ 0.05s), label "just 16 shades" in yellow.
- 24.5s ("clearly the same picture"): the italic line "rougher · same picture · much smaller" fades up.
- 28.1s ("Quantization does exactly this"): both gradient bars dim slightly (opacity .75) and the price/km column dims, leaving the line as the focus.

Scene title fades in at 0.2s.
- 2.7s ("giant pile of numbers called weights"): the 3 input circles and Σ circle pop in (stagger 0.12s), then the three connections draw on from the inputs to Σ (stroke-dashoffset, 0.8s).
- 6.6s ("0.31, or −1.2"): the weight labels 0.31, −1.2, 0.87 fade in on the connections, one per ~0.5s (0.31 at 6.8, −1.2 at 8.2, 0.87 at 9.0).
- 10.8s ("multiplies its inputs ... adds them up"): small blue pulses travel along each connection into Σ (a dot moving along the line, 0.8s each, staggered 0.2s), Σ flashes ink→yellow→ink.
- 16.7s ("Billions of times"): the 8×7 decimal grid at right fills in a fast waterfall (row by row, total ≤ 1.2s), then the whole grid subtly scales 1.0→0.96 to suggest "many more".
- 18.2s ("size of a model is simply..."): the equation "model size = # weights × bits per weight" writes in term by term: "model size =" at 18.4, "# weights" (blue) at 20.3, "×" at 21.5, "bits per weight" (yellow) at 22.0.

Scene title "A bit is a light switch" fades in at 0.2s.
- 0.6s: row "1 bit" appears with its single switch (off). At 4.6s the switch flips on (knob slides from bottom to top, fill dim→yellow, 0.3s) and back off at 5.6s, then on again at 6.6s; "→ 2 values" pops at 7.5s.
- 9.7s ("second switch ... 4 combinations"): row "2 bits" appears; its switches flip through 00,01,10,11 (0.35s each) then "→ 4 values" pops at 11.4s.
- 12.6s ("Three switches, eight"): row "3 bits" appears with "→ 8 values".
- 14.7s ("doubles the count"): the counts column 2, 4, 8 each pulse yellow briefly in sequence.
- 17.5s ("2ᵇ"): the big "2ᵇ" writes in at right with "values" beneath and "each switch doubles it" (dim) at 20.0s.
- 21.1s ("4 bits gives 16"): row "4 bits" appears with "→ 16 values".
- 22.9s ("8 bits, 256"): row "8 bits" appears with "→ 256 values".
- 25.2s ("16 bits, about 65,000"): a small dim line "16 bits → 65,536" appears beneath the stack (y≈740, mono 30px).
- 28.2s ("Every bit you remove halves"): the 8-bit row's last switch fades to 30% and its count briefly shows "128" in red then returns to 256 (demonstrating halving), 1.6s total.

Scene title "How many bits per number?" fades in at 0.2s.
- 0.4s ("FP32, uses 32 bits"): the FP32 strip builds cell by cell left→right (stagger 0.04s), "FP32" label first; "280 GB" counts up at right at 3.5s.
- 5.0s ("one for the sign, 8 for the size, 23"): the three groups tint in order: sign cell red at 5.1, exponent cells yellow at 6.3, mantissa cells blue at 8.0, each with its small label beneath.
- 12.8s ("FP16"): FP16 row builds (it reads as the strip collapsing to half), "140 GB" at right.
- 23.5s ("INT8 ... 256"): INT8 row builds in pink, "256 values" then "70 GB".
- 28.3s ("INT4 ... just 16"): INT4 row builds, "16 values", "35 GB ✓" in teal.
- 31.2s ("70 billion weights at 4 bits"): the italic line "70 billion × 4 bits ≈ 35 GB" writes in; at 34.5s ("Suddenly, it fits") the INT4 row and "35 GB ✓" pulse teal once.

Scene title "Snap every dot to its nearest tick" fades in at 0.2s.
- 2.2s ("dots on a number line"): the axis line draws left→right (1.0s); the 34 blue dots fade in at their raw scattered positions (faint, as in the sketch's ghost dots but at full opacity first), stagger ≤ 0.5s total, with a gentle independent float (±4px sine, finite) on each.
- 7.4s ("lay down a ruler"): the 16 ticks drop in from above (y −40 → 0, back.out, stagger 0.04s).
- 11.1s ("say 16, evenly spaced"): tick indices 0–15 pop in pink beneath (stagger 0.03s).
- 14.6s ("snapping every dot to its nearest tick"): THE signature move — each dot slides along a short straight path from its raw position down to its nearest tick, stacking (as in the sketch), stagger 0.06s, power2.inOut 0.7s each; the raw position stays behind as a 25% ghost with a dashed connector (draw the connectors as the dots move).
- 18.3s ("store which tick it landed on"): "store the tick number, not the exact value" (italic) fades up.
- 23.1s ("a small integer from 0 to 15"): "0.4817… → tick 7" types in; tick 7 and its index pulse pink.
- 29.7s ("choosing the ruler well"): the ticks brighten (ink → yellow) briefly and settle.

Scene title "Step 1 · the scale s" fades in at 0.2s. Ruler at y=470, x 260→1660 (same as sketch).
- 0.4s ("Here are 6 weights"): the six blue dots drop in onto their values with labels −1, −0.43, 0, 0.51, 1.37, 2 (stagger 0.25s).
- 4.0s ("smallest is −1, largest is 2"): the −1 dot and the 2 dot pulse (scale 1→1.4→1) one after another.
- 6.9s ("16 ticks, numbered 0 to 15"): the 16 ticks pop up from the axis (stagger 0.04s).
- 11.2s ("15 gaps"): the 15 gaps highlight one after another as yellow segments flickering along the axis (stagger 0.08s), then fade to nothing except the first gap.
- 15.1s ("full range is 2 − (−1) = 3"): the range brace draws over the dots (stroke-dashoffset 1.0s) and "range = 2 − (−1) = 3" writes in above it.
- 18.4s ("shared across 15 gaps, gives a step of 0.2"): the first gap's yellow bar + "one step" label appear; the equation "s = 3 ÷ 15 gaps = 0.2" builds term by term (s at 18.6, "= 3 ÷ 15 gaps" at 19.6, "= 0.2" at 21.3, yellow).
- 22.7s ("called the scale, written s"): the yellow "s" in the equation scales 1→1.25→1.

Scene title "Step 2 · the zero-point z" fades in at 0.2s. Same ruler as frame 07 at y=470 (no dots this time), indices 0–15 shown from t=0 (it continues the previous board).
- 2.4s ("real 0 sits 5 steps up"): five teal hop arcs draw one by one from tick 0 to tick 5 (0.45s each), each with its count number 1…5 popping above.
- 6.5s: the teal vertical marker at tick 5 rises up with label "real 0" (italic).
- 7.1s ("−1 divided by 0.2 is −5. Flip the sign, 5"): the equation "z = −(−1.0 ÷ 0.2) = 5" builds: "z =" at 7.3, "−(−1.0 ÷ 0.2)" at 8.4, "= 5" (teal) at 11.4.
- 13.1s ("zero-point, z"): the "z" pulses.
- 19.5s ("Keeping 0 exact matters"): the teal pill "0 stays exactly 0" draws on (stroke) and its text fades in.

Scene title "Step 3 · quantize" fades in at 0.2s.
- 0.4s → 8.0s: the formula "q = round( x / s ) + z" writes in by parts as it is spoken: "x / s" at 1.6 ("divide by the scale"), "round( … )" at 4.6, "+ z" at 6.0, "q =" at 8.0. Colours per role.
- 11.3s ("Take 0.51"): the chain row at y≈440 builds token by token on the voice: "0.51" at 11.4, "÷ 0.2" at 13.0, "2.55" at 14.6, "round → 3" at 16.5, "+ 5" at 17.6, "8" at 18.3 (pink, bold, pops).
- 19.5s: in the table below, the x row shows all six values dimmed, and column "0.51" lights up with q=8 popping under it.
- 22.7s ("Let's check two more"): the chain row cross-fades its numbers (old values fade out up 10px, new ones in) to: "−0.43 → ÷ 0.2 → −2.15 → round → −2 → + 5 → 3" with tokens on 23.9 / 25.4 / 27.0 / 29.1 / 30.4 / 31.0; then column −0.43 lights with q=3.
- 32.2s: chain swaps again to "1.37 → ÷ 0.2 → 6.85 → round → 7 → + 5 → 12" (tokens on 32.2 / 34.0 / 35.4 / 36.9 / 38.0 / 38.6); column 1.37 lights with q=12.
- 39.4s ("Do this for every weight"): remaining q values (0, 5, 15) waterfall in; at 43.0s the whole q row pulses pink once, and "each q fits in 4 bits" (dim) fades in at 46.0.

Scene title "Step 4 · back again, and the error" fades in at 0.2s.
- 0.4s → 6.0s: formula "x̂ = s · ( q − z )" writes in by parts on the voice ("( q − z )" at 2.6, "s ·" at 4.4, "x̂ =" at 5.6).
- 6.8s ("8 minus 5 is 3. 3 times 0.2 is 0.6"): "0.2 × (8 − 5) = 0.6" builds in two steps (to "(8 − 5)" at 6.9, "= 0.6" at 9.6).
- 11.7s ("We stored 0.51, got back 0.6"): the zoomed ruler 0.4–0.8 draws; the blue 0.51 dot appears at 12.4, then a short animated snap toward the 0.6 tick leaves the red error bar drawing between them (13.6), "error 0.09" fades in at 14.4.
- 17.0s ("whole list"): the table on the right fills: q row first, then x̂ row values cascade in left→right during 19.9–24.5 matching the spoken list, then the dim x row underneath fades in at 24.8.
- 27.7s ("round to the nearest tick"): the light-red ±s/2 band fades in around the 0.6 tick.
- 29.7s ("never more than half a step... 0.1"): "error ≤ s/2 = 0.1" writes in (red italic), the band edges flash.
- 35.1s ("Every single weight within 0.1"): "every weight within 0.1" fades in under the table; each x̂/x column pair briefly underlines in red in sequence (stagger 0.1s).

Scene title "Why small errors don't pile up" fades in at 0.2s.
- 5.5s ("multiplies each input by a weight, and adds"): column headers "input · exact w · rounded ŵ · error in product" fade in.
- 10.8s ("our 6 weights and 6 inputs"): the six rows' input and exact-w cells waterfall in (stagger 0.15s).
- 13.7s ("With the exact weights, the total is 1"): the blue "Σ = 1.00" counts up from 0.00 to 1.00 (1.2s).
- 16.2s ("rounded weights, the total is also 1"): the rounded ŵ column waterfalls in (stagger 0.12s), then the pink "Σ = 1.00" counts up to 1.00.
- 19.1s ("Look at the errors"): the error column fills: zeros dim, +0.06 at 20.6, +0.03 at 22.0 (both "too high", red), −0.09 at 23.1 ("too low").
- 24.5s ("they cancelled out"): the three red errors fly down into the sum line "+0.06 − 0.09 + 0.03 = 0" which writes in at y=770; the "= 0" pops.
- 28.0s: "errors mostly cancel" (dim mono) fades in at right.
- 34.7s ("the sums to be about right"): "the sum / is what matters" (italic, right) fades up; at 37.0 the two Σ values pulse together.

No top-left title; two headers "Asymmetric" (left) and "Symmetric" (right) fade in at 0.4s and 8.8s respectively; the faint centre divider draws top→bottom at 8.6s.
- 0.4s: left ruler (−1 … 2, 16 ticks) slides in from the left (it is the same ruler as frames 07–08, now smaller); "−1" and "2" labels.
- 3.2s ("lopsided, −1 to 2, zero-point shifts"): teal z marker rises at tick 5 with "z = 5"; left formula "q = round(x/s) + z" writes in at 6.0.
- 12.1s ("Balance the range around 0, from minus... to plus"): right ruler draws outward from its centre (both halves grow from x=1440), labels "−2" and "2" appear at the ends at 14.0 and 15.4.
- 17.1s ("pin the zero-point at 0"): teal "z = 0" marker rises at the centre.
- 19.0s ("integers −7 to 7"): small pink indices −7 … 7 flash under the right ruler then fade to 40%.
- 22.7s ("scale is 2 ÷ 7 ≈ 0.29"): "INT4: −7…7 · s = 2/7 ≈ 0.29" (yellow mono) writes in under the right formula.
- 28.4s ("formula is just q = round(x / s)"): right formula writes in.
- 34.4s ("ticks below −1 are wasted"): the left quarter of the right ruler's ticks dim to 35% and "wasted" (red) fades in beneath.
- 38.5s ("Weights ... symmetric"): "weights → usually" fades in under the right side; 42.0s ("Activations ... asymmetric"): "activations → often" under the left.

Scene title "The real enemy: one outlier" fades in at 0.2s.
- 3.4s ("most weights live between −1 and 1"): 22 blue dots appear clustered over the left of the ruler. Start state: the ruler spans only −1 … 1 (16 ticks evenly across x 200→1700, dots spread across it — precision looks fine).
- 6.5s ("one strange weight is 10"): the red dot slides in from the right edge to x≈1700 with label "10".
- 9.4s ("stretch from −1 all the way to 10"): THE signature move — the ruler re-scales: ticks spread out to the sketch spacing (100px apart, x 200→1700), while the blue dots compress toward the left end (x mapped by (v+1)/11·1500+200), over 2.5s power1.inOut. Everything moves together as one transform of the number line.
- 13.6s ("range of 11, 15 steps, each about 0.73"): the equation "s = (10 − (−1)) ÷ 15 ≈ 0.73" writes in; the 0.73 counts up from 0.13 to 0.73.
- 19.8s ("lands on one of just 3 ticks"): the dots snap to the 3 leftmost ticks (stack), the red rounded box draws around them and "only 3 ticks" fades in.
- 24.6s ("0.1, 0.2, and 0.3 all become the same"): "0.1 → 0", "0.2 → 0", "0.3 → 0" appear one per 1.2s; at 28.6 "same integer — the detail is gone" (red italic) fades up.

Scene title "The fix: more rulers" fades in at 0.2s.
- 0.6s: the three 6×8 weight matrices fade/scale in together (0.95→1), each with the red outlier cell at row 2, col 5.
- 2.5s ("Per-tensor ... one scale for an entire layer"): left matrix: yellow outer border draws on, then the red damage tint floods the whole matrix (opacity 0→0.10); label "per-tensor" + "1 scale · outlier hurts all".
- 8.0s ("Per-channel ... every row its own scale"): middle matrix: six yellow row borders draw top→bottom (stagger 0.1s); label at 8.6.
- 11.8s ("outlier only hurts its own row"): red tint appears only on row 2 of the middle matrix.
- 14.6s ("Per-group ... every small block, 128 weights"): right matrix: 3×4 yellow block borders draw (stagger 0.05s); label at 15.2; at 19.0 the red tint fills only the outlier's block.
- 20.7s ("only ruins its own little neighbourhood"): the three red tints pulse once in sequence left→right, making the shrinking damage obvious.
- 28.5s ("about ⅛ of a bit more per weight"): "cost: ≈ 1/8 bit per weight" fades in.

Scene title "When do you quantize?" fades in at 0.2s.
- 3.4s ("Post-training quantization, or PTQ"): "PTQ" label (yellow) appears; box "train ✓" draws at 4.0.
- 8.7s ("weights ... easy"): arrow → draws.
- 12.1s ("Activations change ... sample sentences"): "calibrate (samples)" box draws (blue); inside it, three small blue dots stream left→right twice (finite).
- 17.1s ("typical ranges. That's called calibration."): arrow → and "quantize" box (pink) draw.
- 21.6s ("quick, needs no retraining"): "fast · no retraining" fades in.
- 24.8s ("Quantization-aware training, or QAT"): "QAT" label (teal) and the long box "train with fake rounding ↺" draw; the ↺ rotates one full turn at 27.0 (finite, 1.2s).
- 30.3s: arrow and "quantize" box draw on the QAT row.
- 32.8s ("better accuracy at very low bits"): "more work · better at low bits" fades in.
- 36.8s ("Just the weights, saves memory"): blue pill "weights only → less memory" draws on.
- 40.6s ("weights and activations together ... integer math"): yellow pill "+ activations → integer math" draws on.

Scene title "The same ideas, inside real tools" fades in at 0.2s.
- Cards rise one per name as it is spoken (y +40 → 0, opacity 0→1, 0.6s power2.out), each card's three mono lines typing in after the title:
  - GPTQ (yellow) at 2.6s; lines at 3.4 / 6.7 / 8.0.
  - AWQ (teal) at 10.7s; lines at 11.5 / 13.4 / 16.2.
  - GGUF (blue) at 17.4s; lines at 18.4 / 21.0 / 24.9.
  - bitsandbytes (pink) at 27.4s; lines at 28.0 / 29.3 / 30.5.
- When a new card arrives, the previous card dims to 55% opacity (the active card stays lit). At 31.8s all four return to 100%.

Scene title "What do you gain, and lose?" fades in at 0.2s.
- 0.4s: the baseline axis draws; the 16-bit bar (140 GB) grows.
- 2.7s ("16 bits to 8 halves the memory"): the 8-bit bar grows (70 GB).
- 7.5s ("4 bits cuts it to a quarter"): the 4-bit bar grows (35 GB).
- 10.9s ("Below that, at 3 or 2 bits"): the 3-bit and 2-bit bars grow (26 GB, 18 GB).
- Quality line: the yellow polyline draws left→right in segments as each bit-width is discussed: 16→8 segment at 4.5, 8→4 at 9.0, then 4→3→2 at 12.5 — visibly falling off the cliff ("falls off fast"). Legend "quality" / "memory" fades in at 4.0.
- Add a small dim mono note "illustrative" under the legend (y≈280) at 4.0 — the curve is illustrative, not measured.
- 16.5s ("faster answers"), 22.2s ("lower cost, less energy"), 24.3s ("your own phone"): the right-side list items appear in order: "faster" at 16.6, "cheaper" at 22.3, "less energy" at 23.4, "on your phone" at 24.4.

No title. FINAL SCENE: a settle/fade at the very end is allowed.
- 0.4s: the ruler from frame 06 returns (axis draws, ticks pop, stagger 0.03s) with the six blue dots snapping onto their ticks (callback).
- Recipe lines stack one per sentence (symbol pops first in its colour, then the text writes in):
  - "s · pick a range, split it into steps" at 2.0s
  - "z · mark where zero lives" at 7.4s
  - "q · divide · round · shift → store" at 11.4s
  - "x̂ · multiply back when needed" at 15.5s
- 28.6s ("Quantization is rounding, done cleverly."): the closing yellow italic line writes in (characters fade in left→right over 1.4s). This is the film's held frame: from 30.5s nothing moves except a 4px drift.
- 34.7s → end: everything fades to 0 over 2.0s (final scene only).
